hypothesis: fixed incremental rig rotations plus correspondence-reestimated pair directions and independent per-edge scales can remove segment-scale translation drift without changing registration or map support

configuration.reference_sensor: sensor closest to the rig origin; must be within 1e-6 m
configuration.direction_estimator: smallest fixed-rotation epipolar nullspace from at most 64 deterministic correspondences
configuration.connectivity_backbone: unit-weight consecutive registered-frame directions from the current trajectory; edge scales remain independent
configuration.complexity: O(frames + verified correspondences + sparse edges); no image-pair matrix
configuration.publication: Sim(3)-align to the current gauge, cap the maximum pose update, fixed-rotation structure refinement, then transactional support and reprojection guards

decision.reason: the fully connected 1k proposal retained only 7.57% of tracks and 36.89% of observations while increasing reprojection error by 117.29%; both independent publication guards failed
decision.interpretation: pairwise translation directions in the corridor do not provide a consistent segment-scale solution under this sparse independent-scale formulation; adding a current-trajectory backbone establishes connectivity but does not make the accepted long edges geometrically compatible
decision.next_action: retain this default-off bounded diagnostic and move the quality investigation to temporal localization of track/topology residuals around the first 10k drift segment before proposing another pose solver
